Although remarkable progress has been achieved, the current AAC system outputs are far from accurate, detailed, diverse and useful to humans. There are still several crucial challenges to be tackled, such as re-evaluating new metrics, knowledge transfer, model compression, diverse/controllable captioning, detailed captioning, and revisiting the definition of AAC.
papers.rule: There are still several crucial challenges to be tackled. We discuss some potential research directions to encourage novel works. The survey is meant to provide a comprehensive introduction and insights about this task to new researchers.

papers.gold: The proposed multi-view correlation consistency (MVCC) approach outperforms its consistency learning only and contrastive learning variants. This approach additionally contains a view-coherent data augmentation strategy for the dense prediction task, which allows for differentiable and invertible image-level geometric augmentation and view-coherent region-level augmentation. In a series of semi-supervised settings, our method has very competitive performance compared with the state of the art.
papers.rule: We integrate this supervision signal in a multi-view correlation consistency (MVCC) approach, which is shown to outperform its consistency learning only and contrastive learning variants. This approach additionally contains a view-coherent data augmentation strategy for the dense prediction task, which allows for differentiable and invertible image-level geometric augmentation and view-coherent region-level augmentation. In a series of semi-supervised settings, our method has very competitive performance compared with the state of the art.

papers.gold: The KG-based models outperform other methods focusing on black box strategies or explainability in terms of F1-score. The inclusion of fuzzy rules enhances the robustness of the KG and provides additional evidence for Bayesian inference.

Finally, explainable descriptions of the behavioral predictions have been implemented using Retrieval Augmented Generation Techniques (RAG), as a means to combine the reasoning ability of Knowledge Graphs and the expressive capacity of Large Language Models. Despite the progress exhibited in the current work, a number of improvements are envisaged with a view to extending and testing the predictive capabilities in new use cases, such as: 1) near-miss (or crash) lane change maneuvers, and 2) occluded children on urban scenarios.

papers.gold: The authors release the first large-scale FAS dataset based on surveillance scenes, SuHiFiMask, and propose the CQIL network. Comprehensive experiments verify the importance of the datasets for the FAS task and the effectiveness of the proposed method.
papers.rule: In addition, we propose a Contrastive Quality-Invariance Learning (CQIL) network to recover image information using super-resolution and enhance the robustness of the algorithm to quality variations by fitting the quality variance distribution. Finally, we conduct comprehensive experiments on SuHiFiMask and three other datasets to verify the importance of the datasets for the FAS task and the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers.gold: Feature representations pre-trained through reconstruction yield a notable enhancement in OOD detection and narrow the performance gap among various score functions. Even simple score functions can rival complex ones when leveraging reconstruction-based pretext tasks. MOODv2 employs the masked image modeling pretext task and achieves remarkable enhancements on both ImageNet and CIFAR-10.
papers.rule: This implies that even simple score functions can perform as well as complex ones when utilizing reconstruction-based pretext tasks. These findings hold promise for further development in OOD detection. Ultimately, we introduce the MOODv2 OOD detection framework, employing the masked image modeling pretext task, which achieves a remarkable [MATH] increase in AUROC, reaching [MATH] on ImageNet, and substantially improving CIFAR-10 to [MATH] .

papers.gold: The fusion of features from cross-modalities facilitates the generation of reliable geometries to complete partial point clouds. Features learned from images not only constrain the generation of the overall shape of an object but also help to refine its local details.
papers.rule: Our work has revealed that the fusion of features from cross-modalities facilitates the generation of reliable geometries to complete partial point clouds. This benefits from the fact that features learned from images not only constrain the generation of the overall shape of an object but also help to refine its local details, indicating the potential of using images to recover finer geometry of objects from partial point clouds.

papers.gold: Utilizing a scene graph is the most effective way of informing the LLMs of the proper scene context and semantic information for scene understanding and spatial reasoning. The proposed LLM-based method identifies over 90% of anomalous scenarios in the dataset.
papers.rule: We also propose an LLM-based approach that utilizes a scene graph and classification approach. This methods identifies over [MATH] of anomalous scenarios in our dataset. Additionally, we show that these techniques remain viable in the real world.

papers.gold: The proposed method of formulating language-driven appearance knowledge units via an LLM and incorporating them with visual cues effectively improves pedestrian detection performance across various frameworks, achieving state-of-the-art results on public benchmarks.
papers.rule: Through task-prompting, we acquire appearance knowledge units which are representative and become relevant with pedestrian detection. Finally, we provided language-driven appearance knowledge by incorporating the units with visual cues in a pedestrian detector. With extensive experiments, we verified the effectiveness of our method showing state-of-the-art performances.

papers.gold: Images are often redundant in non-noisy settings when using a strong text-based baseline. Visual context is valuable when the source text is noisy, with cropped image features being best for low-noise and full image features for high-noise. However, improvements were not due to useful information from images but because images act as noise making the model more robust. Datasets where the image is necessary are needed for models to learn to use visual features effectively.
papers.rule: We show that the models need to use images more effectively, even when noise is introduced in the text, making it less adequate. This could be changed with the usage of datasets where the image is necessary, enabling models to learn to use visual features effectively. In the future, we would like to explore the effectiveness of multilingual multimodal NMT for some other languages and datasets under noisy settings.
